title: Step the calendar grid from noon so midnight DST changes cannot shift it
head: d533f5a1fc1a
workflow: Opus full review, Sol boundary hunter, Opus self-check of the draft, editorial check, batch gates

leads.summary: A calendar day removed by a date-line change still breaks the noon-anchored grid
leads.consequence: In Pacific/Apia December 2011, row five reads 26,27,28,29,31,1,2 instead of 26,27,28,29,30,31,1: Saturday the 31st is painted under Friday, and following cells/weekday columns shift; the historical December 30 cannot appear in the grid. This is a historical date-line edge case, not the ordinary Chile 2026 DST fix. Five affected zones/dates were confirmed with the actual head under Node: Apia and Fakaofo 2011-12-30; Kanton and Kiritimati 1994-12-31; Kwajalein 1993-08-21. Building and walking civil grid dates in UTC, then returning day keys rather than local Date objects, avoids requiring a local noon for a day that was entirely skipped.
leads.triage: corroborated_not_published; Opus final lists the same day-skip zones; base and head render identically, pre-existing and historical.

leads.summary: Both new assertions pass when a plausible cursor regression restores midnight
leads.consequence: A diagnostic copy of the reviewed Model.js that inserts cursor.setHours(0) before each cursor.setDate keeps the two exact noon strings in place, and the full clock-test.sh passes under Node, including the Santiago date/weekday assertion. This restores the Qt missing-midnight hazard because setDate runs from midnight. The Chile behavioural check by itself also passes in UTC if TZ is not applied; there is no assertion that Santiago timezone is active. A QV4-engine test with a non-GUI core application, or a stronger property-oriented test that actually rejects local-clock arithmetic, is needed to catch this specific regression; at minimum assert the cursor remains at noon when it is advanced rather than matching source substrings only.
leads.triage: corroborated; Same weakness as the published pin finding (pin is the only guard under Node); Opus showed a midnight cursor passes the Chile check. Published via the commented-revert reproducer instead.

leads.summary: Exact local-noon source pin collides with two active UTC calendar fixes
leads.consequence: Open PRs #10476 and #13186 both solve the same grid bug using UTC and add tests. They are diverged, not stacked on #13627. The two files have merge conflict markers when merging from each other's own base, and resolving by retaining either UTC grid makes this PR's new source assertion fail even though the UTC models include Apia's skipped date. Conversely leaving #13627's code in place fails #10476's no-local-Date assertion and #13186's skipped-date assertion. Coordinate a single implementation and remove or adapt mutually exclusive tests rather than combining all three unchanged. GitHub reports those PRs individually mergeable against their own base, not a clean sequential merge of these alternatives.
leads.triage: confirmed_published; Coordinator verified #10476 and #13186 (UTC) and #12943, #12985, #13096, #13127 (noon) with gh pr view/diff; Opus confirmed in self-check (opus/upstream/related-check/). Merge conflict stated as likely, not tested by coordinator.

leads.summary: Unset TZ is not restored after the new test's timezone override
leads.consequence: When the runner did not set TZ, `const zone = process.env.TZ` saves undefined but `process.env.TZ = zone` sets the literal string 'undefined'; the remaining checks now run in a different environment (UTC fallback in the pinned Node) and future tests in the same child may silently exercise the wrong zone. Existing subsequent assertions do pass, and no parent-shell environment or production configuration is changed. Delete process.env.TZ when zone === undefined (and use finally for exception safety if tests are added between override/restore).

comment:
## Automated AI review

> **Community review:** Independent automated community review, unaffiliated with the Omarchy team, intended to help prepare PRs for their review.

**Outcome:** Six other open PRs fix the same bug, and the new pin still passes when the fix is reverted but the noon lines are left as comments.

### Six other open PRs fix this

#12943 makes the same two-line code change, #12985, #13096 and #13127 also use noon, and #10476 (the earliest) and #13186 build the grid in UTC. All edit `monthGrid()` and `clock-test.sh`, so the first to merge will likely conflict with the rest.

**Suggested change:** Link the related PRs so maintainers can pick one.

### The pin accepts a commented fix

Under Node the Chile check cannot catch this regression, so the pin is the only guard. It reads `Model.js` with comments intact, so a revert that keeps the noon lines as comments passes.

**Suggested change:** Strip comment lines from `modelSource`, as the file already does for `BarWidget.qml`.

<details><summary>Reproducer</summary>

# Reproducer: the noon pin in clock-test.sh accepts the fix left behind as a comment

Reviewed head: `d533f5a1fc1aaecbece47bfac8750f0cf21fdb2f`.

The new Chile check in `test/shell.d/clock-test.sh` cannot fail under Node (V8 resolves the missing midnight forward, as the PR description says), so the source-text pin is the only thing guarding the fix. The pin reads `Model.js` with its comments intact, so a revert that leaves the noon lines behind as comments still passes the whole file. The same test file already strips comments from `BarWidget.qml` for exactly this reason (lines 11-14).

## Steps

From a checkout of the PR head, put both lines back to midnight and keep the noon versions as comments:

```diff
--- shell/plugins/panels/clock/Model.js
+++ shell/plugins/panels/clock/Model.js
@@ -236,8 +236,10 @@
   // Noon, not midnight: where DST starts at midnight that local midnight does
   // not exist, and QML's engine resolves it back into the previous day, so a
   // midnight cursor repeated that day and shifted every later cell.
-  var leading = (new Date(year, month, 1, 12).getDay() - start + 7) % 7
-  var cursor = new Date(year, month, 1 - leading, 12)
+  // var leading = (new Date(year, month, 1, 12).getDay() - start + 7) % 7
+  var leading = (new Date(year, month, 1).getDay() - start + 7) % 7
+  // var cursor = new Date(year, month, 1 - leading, 12)
+  var cursor = new Date(year, month, 1 - leading)
   var today = String(todayKey || "")
   var weeks = []
```

Then run the file:

```sh
bash test/shell.d/clock-test.sh; echo "exit=$?"
```

## Actual output (Node v26.7.0)

The run exits 0. The two new checks report:

```
ok - calendar steps its grid from noon so a midnight DST change cannot move it across a day
ok - calendar lists each day once under its weekday across a midnight DST change
```

and the file ends with:

```
ok - default bar layout includes the clock widget
ok - SUPER+CTRL+ALT+D toggles the calendar panel
```

Controls from the same runs: the head test run against the base `Model.js` (both lines at midnight, no comment copies) fails the pin as intended (`not ok - calendar steps its grid from noon so a midnight DST change cannot move it across a day`, exit 1), and so does a head `Model.js` with only the cursor line put back to midnight. A behaviourally identical rewrite of the cursor line, `new Date(year, month, 1 - leading, 12, 0)`, also fails the pin, because it matches exact text.

## Suggested change

Read `Model.js` the way the file already reads `BarWidget.qml`, with comment lines stripped, before the `includes` checks:

```js
const modelSource = fs.readFileSync(root + '/shell/plugins/panels/clock/Model.js', 'utf8')
  .replace(/^\s*\/\/.*$/gm, '')
```

</details>

<details><summary>Verified</summary>

- Qt 6.11.2 QML engine (`qml -a core`): the base grid for `America/Santiago`, September 2026, prints `31/Mo 1/Tu 2/We 3/Th 4/Fr 5/Sa 5/Sa`, as in the description; the head prints each day once under its weekday.
- The head also fixes the same repeat in `America/Havana`, `Africa/Cairo`, `Asia/Beirut` and `Atlantic/Azores`, whose rules start DST at 00:00.
- A scan of all 341 system zones for 1900–2040 (weeks starting Monday, Sunday and Saturday) found no month the head renders wrong that the base rendered right.
- `Europe/Berlin`, `America/New_York` and UTC render identically before and after.
- `clock-test.sh` passes at the head, and fails at the pin against the base `Model.js`.

</details>

<details><summary>Details: harness used to verify the fix</summary>

## Harness

Save as `check.qml` at the root of each checkout:

```qml

import "shell/plugins/panels/clock/Model.js" as Model

// Prints a month grid (weeks start Monday) as the shell's own JavaScript
// engine computes it. Usage: qml -a core check.qml -- <year> <month 1-12>
QtObject {
  Component.onCompleted: {
    var args = Qt.application.arguments
    var rest = args.slice(args.indexOf("--") + 1)
    var names = ["Su", "Mo", "Tu", "We", "Th", "Fr", "Sa"]
    Model.monthGrid(Number(rest[0]), Number(rest[1]) - 1, 1, "").forEach(function(week) {
      console.log("W" + week.week + ": " + week.days.map(function(day) {
        return day.day + "/" + names[day.weekday]
      }).join(" "))
    })
    Qt.exit(0)
  }
}
```

```sh

TZ=Africa/Cairo /usr/lib/qt6/bin/qml -a core check.qml -- 2026 4
```

<details><summary>More findings</summary>

### Heading and month stepping still use midnight on the 1st (pre-existing)

`Panel.qml` `viewDate` and `stepMonth()` in `Model.js` still build local midnight on the 1st. **Impact:** in Qt's engine, where DST started at 00:00 on a 1st in zones such as Havana (April 2012), the heading reads MARCH and stepping never reaches April. Under current tz rules no zone hits this from 2015 through 2040.

**Suggested change:** Anchor both at noon, as #13096 and #13127 already do (#10476 moves `stepMonth()` to UTC).

</details>

<details><summary>Reproducer: heading and month stepping</summary>

# Reproducer: the heading and month stepping still build local midnight on the 1st

Reviewed head: `d533f5a1fc1aaecbece47bfac8750f0cf21fdb2f`. Engine: Qt 6.11.2 QML (`qml -a core`, a QCoreApplication, no window).

The PR moves the grid off midnight, but two other places in the clock panel still construct midnight on the first of the month:

- `Panel.qml` line 43: `readonly property date viewDate: new Date(viewYear, viewMonth, 1)`, which names the heading (line 726, `Qt.formatDate(root.viewDate, "MMMM yyyy")`).
- `Model.js` line 280: `stepMonth()` uses `new Date(year, Number(month) + Number(delta), 1)`, which drives the chevrons, wheel, arrow keys and `[`/`]`/`{`/`}`.

When DST starts at 00:00 on a 1st, the QML engine resolves that missing midnight back to 23:00 on the last day of the previous month, the same way it did for the grid cursor. Under tzdata 2026c no zone's current rules put a midnight DST start on a 1st, so today this only shows when browsing back to such a month. Example: Cuba started DST at 00:00 on 2012-04-01 (`Rule Cuba 2012 only - Apr 1 0:00s 1:00 D`).

## Steps

Save as `heading.qml` at the root of a checkout of the PR head:

```qml
import QtQml
import "shell/plugins/panels/clock/Model.js" as Model

// Mirrors Panel.qml: viewDate (line 43), its heading (line 726) and
// moveMonth's Model.stepMonth. Usage: qml -a core heading.qml -- <year> <month 1-12>
QtObject {
  id: root
  property int viewYear: 0
  property int viewMonth: 0
  readonly property date viewDate: new Date(viewYear, viewMonth, 1)

  Component.onCompleted: {
    var args = Qt.application.arguments
    var rest = args.slice(args.indexOf("--") + 1)
    root.viewYear = Number(rest[0])
    root.viewMonth = Number(rest[1]) - 1
    console.log("heading for month " + rest[1] + ": " + Qt.formatDate(root.viewDate, "MMMM yyyy").toUpperCase())
    var prev = Model.stepMonth(root.viewYear, root.viewMonth, -1)
    console.log("next month from " + (prev.month + 1) + "/" + prev.year + ": " + JSON.stringify(Model.stepMonth(prev.year, prev.month, 1)))
    var next = Model.stepMonth(root.viewYear, root.viewMonth, 1)
    console.log("previous month from " + (next.month + 1) + "/" + next.year + ": " + JSON.stringify(Model.stepMonth(next.year, next.month, -1)))
    Qt.exit(0)
  }
}
```

Run from the checkout root with Arch's Qt 6 `qml` tool. `QT_FORCE_STDERR_LOGGING=1` keeps `console.log` on stderr when it is not a terminal, and `QT_MESSAGE_PATTERN='%{message}'` drops the `qml:` prefix; the runs below also had `QML_DISABLE_DISK_CACHE=1`:

```sh
export QT_FORCE_STDERR_LOGGING=1 QT_MESSAGE_PATTERN='%{message}' QML_DISABLE_DISK_CACHE=1
TZ=America/Havana /usr/lib/qt6/bin/qml -a core heading.qml -- 2012 4
TZ=America/New_York /usr/lib/qt6/bin/qml -a core heading.qml -- 2012 4
```

## Actual output

`stepMonth` returns a zero-based month, so `"month":2` is March and `"month":3` is April.

`TZ=America/Havana`, April 2012:

```
heading for month 4: MARCH 2012
next month from 3/2012: {"year":2012,"month":2}
previous month from 5/2012: {"year":2012,"month":2}
```

`TZ=America/New_York`, April 2012 (control):

```
heading for month 4: APRIL 2012
next month from 3/2012: {"year":2012,"month":3}
previous month from 5/2012: {"year":2012,"month":3}
```

In Havana the April 2012 heading reads MARCH, "next" from March stays on March and "previous" from May skips to March, so stepping never reaches April 2012. The grid itself is correct at the head for that month.

## Suggested change

Anchor both at noon, like the grid:

```js
// Model.js stepMonth()
var target = new Date(year, Number(month) + Number(delta), 1, 12)
```

```qml
// Panel.qml
readonly property date viewDate: new Date(viewYear, viewMonth, 1, 12)
```

</details>
